title: Finance & Legal: Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, Revenue Recognition & Billing Policy
author: Michael Chen
content:
Overview:

This document defines Redwood Inference’s consolidated Finance & Legal policies for annual budgeting and rolling forecasting, procurement and vendor onboarding, contract review and signature authorities, and revenue recognition and billing practices. The intent is to provide a single reference for product, engineering, sales, legal, and operations teams to ensure consistent decision-making and strong internal controls.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood business units, products (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private), and legal entities unless a subsidiary-specific policy is published.
- Covers budgeting cadence, approval gates, procurement thresholds, contract review triggers, revenue recognition rules (ASC 606 aligned), billing cadence, and dispute/credit procedures.

Key contacts and ownership:
- Finance (owner): finance-legal team (Primary contact: Michael Chen, Head of Finance Operations).
- Legal (review): Legal Team (Primary contact: Priya Kaur, General Counsel).
- Procurement & Vendor Management: Procurement Lead (Ethan Morales).
- Billing & RevRec operations: Revenue Operations (Sofia Rivera).

1) Budgeting and Forecasting

Objective:
Provide an annual budget and a monthly rolling forecast that tie to operational plans, product roadmaps, and capacity commitments (Dedicated capacity and Private deployment contracts).

Annual Budget Calendar (high level):
1. Q3 (Aug–Sep): Leadership planning kickoff and bottom-up requests collected from functional teams.
2. Q4 start (Oct–Nov): Finance consolidates and prepares first draft budget; leadership review and cross-functional trade-offs.
3. Q4 end (Dec): Final budget approved by CFO and CEO; board materials prepared as required.
4. Q1 (Jan): Execute budget, activate headcount requisitions and procurement targets.

Rolling Forecast and Cadence:
- Monthly rolling 12-month forecast maintained by Finance using the standard template. Forecast must include revenue by product (Hosted, Dedicated, Private), cost of goods sold (COGS) by category (GPU cloud spend, instance rental, data storage), operating expenses by function, and cash runway.
- Changes > +/- 5% quarter-over-quarter in revenue or > $250k in OPEX variance require an exception memo and leadership sign-off.

Templates and Inputs:
- Use the canonical budget workbook (Finance folder: /shared/finance/templates/annual-budget-2025.xlsx).
- Product teams must submit 12-month customer commit and pricing assumptions. Sales must provide committed bookings and pipeline coverage.

Budget Approval Matrix (examples):
- Department-level budgets signed by department head and finance manager.
- Cross-functional increases > $250k require CFO approval.
- Capital spend (capex) > $100k requires finance + CTO sign-off and a capex request form.

2) Procurement Procedures (Procure-to-Pay)

Goal:
Ensure cost-effective purchasing while maintaining appropriate controls for vendor risk, security, and contractual obligations.

Vendor Onboarding Checklist:
- Business case and budget code assigned.
- Vendor due diligence: AML/KYC check, security questionnaire (for vendors with data access), and references.
- Procurement onboarding form completed and stored in Procurement Portal (ProcureNow).
- W-9 / tax forms collected for US vendors; VAT registration documentation for EU vendors.

Approval matrix (procurement):
- <= $5,000: Requestor manager approval.
- $5,001–$50,000: Department head + finance manager.
- $50,001–$250,000: Finance Director + Procurement Lead.
- > $250,000: CFO + Legal + VP-level review.

Purchase Orders and Invoicing:
- All purchases above $5,000 require a Purchase Order (PO) before invoicing. POs are issued from the Procurement Portal and must reference the budget code.
- Three-way matching required for invoice payment: PO, supplier invoice, and receiving confirmation (or acceptance via ticket).

Preferred vendor terms and discounts:
- Procurement maintains a preferred vendor list (PVL) including cloud GPU, storage, networking, and third-party SaaS. Procurement negotiates enterprise discounts and term length (preferred: 12 months with automatic renewal opt-out).

3) Contracts and Legal Process

Contract intake and tracking:
- All contracts must be submitted to Legal via Contracts Hub (ContractFlow) with completed intake form. Contract metadata must include counterparty name, estimated ARR/commit, term length, data access, and security classification.
- ContractFlow assigns a tracking ID and owner; key milestones (negotiation, legal approval, signature) are tracked.

Standard Terms & Templates:
- Legal maintains standard templates for: Master Services Agreement (MSA), Statement of Work (SOW), Data Processing Addendum (DPA), NDA, and Reseller Agreement. Use templates unless a deviation is approved by Legal.

Signature authority and delegation:
- Individual contributors: Not authorized to sign.
- Manager-level contracts up to $100k: Sales Manager with Finance acknowledgement and Legal review (if template used).
- > $100k or non-standard terms (data residency, custom indemnities, liability caps, export controls): Legal + CFO sign-off required.
- Exceptions: Only the CEO or CFO can authorize multi-year, enterprise commitments > $2M without Board notification.

Contract review triggers (Legal review required if any of the following):
- Term > 24 months.
- Liability cap exceeds 12 months' revenue or > $1M.
- Any clause with source code escrow or IP assignment.
- Customer requires on-prem deployment with data residency constraints.
- Revenue impact estimated > $250k ARR or impacts accounting treatment (e.g., distinct deliverables).

Redlines, Negotiation, and Approval Steps:
1. Sales uploads proposed contract and redline summary.
2. Legal performs initial review and returns redline + negotiation playbook.
3. Pricing/Finance evaluates revenue & billing impact.
4. Final redline approved by Legal, Finance acknowledges, and authorized signatory executes.

Contract archival and retention:
- Executed contracts are stored in ContractFlow and backed up to the corporate document store. Retention is 7 years from contract expiration for commercial agreements; longer where required by law.

4) Revenue Recognition (RevRec) and Billing Policies

Principles (ASC 606 aligned):
1. Identify the contract(s) with a customer.
2. Identify the performance obligations in the contract.
3. Determine the transaction price.
4. Allocate the transaction price to the performance obligations.
5. Recognize revenue when (or as) performance obligations are satisfied.

Product-specific recognition rules:
- Hosted API (usage-based): Recognize revenue as usage occurs (measured tokens) on a monthly basis; bill in arrears. Any prepayments (prepaid credits) are recorded as deferred revenue and released to revenue as usage is consumed.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): For committed term contracts with a predictable monthly fee, recognize ratably over the contract period unless separate performance obligations exist (e.g., extended onboarding services recognized on completion schedule).
- Private (on-prem / perpetual or term licenses): License fees are recognized per contract terms — perpetual licenses recognized when control transfers (rare); term licenses recognized ratably over term. Implementation services are evaluated for distinct deliverables and recognized based on completion of the service.
- Professional services (integration, custom work): Recognize based on percentage of completion using cost-to-cost or milestone methods as documented in the SOW and approved by Finance.

Billing cadence and invoice terms:
- Usage-based billing (Hosted): Monthly in arrears; invoices issued by the 5th business day after month-end with NET 30 payment terms standard.
- Dedicated reserved capacity: Monthly invoices in advance for the committed capacity unless contract specifies otherwise; annual prepay options supported.
- Private deployments and large enterprise: Milestone-based invoicing per contract (e.g., 30% signing, 40% on delivery, 30% on acceptance).

Credits, disputes, and refunds:
- All billing disputes must be submitted via Finance billing portal within 60 days of invoice. Disputes are triaged by Revenue Operations and Sales.
- Credits for service interruptions are governed by SLA terms; standard hosted SLA credit formula: credit = (downtime minutes / total SLA minutes) * monthly recurring fee, capped per SLA schedule.
- Refunds require CFO approval and must be documented with rationale and GL adjustments.

Deferred revenue, cutoffs, and month-end close:
- Recognize cutoffs per calendar month. Sales and Legal must provide all signed contracts by the 3rd business day of the month to ensure timely recognition and invoicing.
- Deferred revenue roll-forward must be prepared monthly by Revenue Operations and reviewed by Finance.

Collections and delinquency policy:
- Standard term: NET 30. Past due >30 days: account flagged and A/R team initiates collection. >60 days: Sales and Finance engage the customer; potential service interruption for overdue balances >90 days, subject to legal and account plan.

5) Controls, Audit & Monitoring

Segregation of duties:
- Requestors cannot approve their own invoices.
- Different individuals must perform vendor setup, invoice approval, and payment execution.

Audit evidence and retention:
- Supporting docs (PO, contract, invoice, receiving evidence) retained for 7 years (longer where required).
- Quarterly internal audits of high-risk vendor spend and contract compliance.

Key metrics and reporting:
- Monthly: revenue by product line, deferred revenue, DSO (days sales outstanding), aging (>30/60/90), and bad debt reserves.
- Quarterly: variance analysis vs. budget and forecast, significant contract amendments, and major procurement exceptions.

Appendices

A. Example approval matrix (text table):
| Amount Range | Approver(s) | Additional Requirements |
|--------------|-------------|-------------------------|
| <= $5k | Manager | PO optional unless recurring |
| $5k–$50k | Department Head + Finance | PO required |
| $50k–$250k | Finance Director + Procurement | Security questionnaire if data access |
| > $250k | CFO + Legal + VP | Board notification if multi-year > $2M |

B. Sample revenue treatment note:
- Customer signs a 12-month Dedicated capacity contract for $120,000 billed monthly. Revenue recognized ratably at $10,000/month. If the contract includes a separate onboarding SOW for $30,000 payable at start and recognized over 3 months as work completes, Revenue Operations must tag the SOW as a distinct performance obligation.

C. Templates and references:
- Annual budget template: /shared/finance/templates/annual-budget-2025.xlsx
- Standard MSA and SOW templates: ContractFlow -> Templates -> Commercial
- Procurement Portal (ProcureNow) onboarding checklist: /tools/procure/portal/onboarding-checklist

Questions and exceptions:
- Submit policy exception requests via finance-policy-exceptions@redwood.ai with a business justification and mitigation plan.

Revision history:
- 2024-11-01: Initial draft (Michael Chen).
- 2024-12-18: Legal updates to signature authority and contract triggers (Priya Kaur).
- 2025-02-15: Finalized billing cadence and procurement thresholds; published.

This policy is intended to be practical. For edge cases (complex multi-jurisdiction contracts, M&A related procurements, or regulatory data residency requests), engage Legal and Finance early.
